source.author: verg
source.text: Horror ubique animo, simul ipsa silentia terrent.
source.text_original: Horror ubique animo, simul ipsa silentia terrent.
source.text_english: Everywhere there is horror in the mind; at the same time the very silence is terrifying.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Haec porta contra portam. Dum essem Romae puer, et liberalibus studiis erudirer, solebam cum caeteris ejusdem aetatis et propositi, diebus Dominicis sepulcra apostolorum et martyrum circuire; crebroque cryptas ingredi, quae in terrarum profunda defossae, ex utraque parte ingredientium per parietes habent corpora sepultorum, et ita obscura sunt omnia, ut propemodum illud propheticum compleatur: Descendant ad infernum viventes: et raro desuper lumen admissum, horrorem temperet tenebrarum, ut non tam fenestram, quam foramen demissi luminis putes: rursumque pedetentim acceditur, et caeca nocte circumdatis illud Virgilianum proponitur: Horror ubique animos, simul ipsa silentia terrent.
reuse.text_original: Haec porta contra portam.» Dum essem Romae puer, et liberalibus studiis erudirer, solebam cum caeteris ejusdem aetatis et propositi, diebus Dominicis sepulcra apostolorum et martyrum circuire; crebroque cryptas ingredi, quae in terrarum profunda defossae, ex utraque parte ingredientium per parietes habent corpora sepultorum, et ita obscura sunt omnia, ut propemodum illud propheticum compleatur: Descendant ad infernum viventes: et raro desuper lumen admissum, horrorem temperet tenebrarum, ut non tam fenestram, quam foramen demissi luminis putes: rursumque pedetentim acceditur, et caeca nocte circumdatis illud Virgilianum proponitur: Horror ubique animos, simul ipsa silentia terrent.
reuse.text_english: This gate is opposite the gate. While I was a boy in Rome and was being instructed in the liberal studies, I used to go with others of the same age and purpose on the Lord’s days to visit the tombs of the apostles and martyrs; and often I used to enter the crypts, which, dug deep down in the earth, have along the walls on either side of those entering the bodies of the buried, and everything is so dark that nearly that prophetic saying is fulfilled: Let the living go down into hell. And only rarely, from above, is a light admitted to temper the horror of the darkness, so that you would think it not so much a window as a hole through which the light is let down; and then one advances little by little, and, with blind night all around, that line of Virgil is applied: Horror everywhere strikes the mind, and the very silence frightens.
